OK, so `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild` sets `IsTestingPlatformApplication` to `True` if it's empty. And `MSTest.TestAdapter` sets it to `$(EnableMSTestRunner)`. The issue is prop ordering - the MTP MSBuild props runs first and sets it to True (if empty), then the MSTest.TestAdapter props runs after and overwrites it with `$(EnableMSTestRunner)`.

But wait - our evaluation says `EnableMSTestRunner` is `true` but `IsTestingPlatformApplication` is `false`. That's contradictory. Let me look closer. 

Actually, I think I see the problem now. The adapter props file has a condition that only sets `EnableMSTestRunner` to `false` if it's empty, so by the time the adapter props runs, `EnableMSTestRunner` is already `true` from the project file. But then it unconditionally sets `IsTestingPlatformApplication` to that value, which should make it `true`. Unless... the adapter props is running before the MTP props? That would explain why `IsTestingPlatformApplication` ends up `false` - the adapter sets it to `$(EnableMSTestRunner)` which is `true`, but then MTP props runs after and... no wait, MTP only sets it if it's empty, so it wouldn't override.

Hold on - what if the order is actually MTP props first, then adapter props, then our csproj? In that case, when the adapter props runs, `EnableMSTestRunner` would still be empty (not yet set by our csproj), so the adapter would set `IsTestingPlatformApplication` to `false`. Then our csproj sets `EnableMSTestRunner` to `true`, but by then `IsTestingPlatformApplication` has already been locked in as `false`. That's the real issue - the property gets evaluated too early, before our project file has a chance to set the value.

The simplest solution is to just use MSTest.Sdk instead, which handles all of this automatically.
